{{nihongo|'''Oomiwa Shrine'''|大神神社 (大垣市)}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Mino Province]].

'''Ōmiwa Shrine''' (おおみわじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} in Kamiishizu-chō, {{ill|Ōgaki|Q384926|qid=Q384926}}, {{ill|Gifu Prefecture|Q131277|qid=Q131277}}.

It is a {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=shikinaisha}} of Tagi District, {{ill|Mino Province|Q864156|qid=Q864156}}, and its former rank under the {{ill|Q712534|lt=Modern shrine ranking system}} was {{ill|Gō-sha|Q134917316|qid=Q134917316}}. It is one of the many {{ill|Ōmiwa Shrine|Q705542|qid=Q705542}} in Japan.

=== Enshrined deities ===
*{{ill|Ōmononushi|lt=Ōmononushi|Q10936701|qid=Q10936701|qid=Q10936701|lt=Ōmononushi Kushimikatama-no-Mikoto}}

Associated deities
*{{ill|Emperor Jimmu|Q200188|qid=Q200188|lt=Kamuyamatoiwarehiko-no-Sumeramikoto}}
*{{ill|Himetataraisuzu-hime|Q5353793|qid=Q5353793|lt=Himetataraisuzuhime-no-Mikoto}}

=== History ===
*The founding date is unknown. During the reign of {{ill|Empress Jitō|Q232026|qid=Q232026}}, when she reached Yokkaichi District in {{ill|Ise Province|Q864166|qid=Q864166}} on an imperial progress to Ise, Right Minister Miwa no Ason Takachimaro received an oracle from Ōmononushi Kushimikatama-no-Mikoto and founded this shrine on Mt. Tagi in Mino Province. It was originally called Ōmiwa Shrine.
*In {{ill|1113|Q19531|qid=Q19531}} (Eikyū 1), a nearby shrine was washed to this shrine in a violent storm. The deity of that shrine (Emperor Jinmu and Himetataraisuzuhime-no-Mikoto) was merged here, and the name was changed to Nagarehiko Daimyōjin.
*In {{ill|1375|Q6277|qid=Q6277}} (Eiwa 7), it was moved to the current site.
*In {{ill|1869|Q7720|qid=Q7720}} (Meiji 2), it resumed the name Ōmiwa Shrine; in Meiji 6 ({{ill|1873|Q7757|qid=Q7757}}), it became gōsha.

=== Cultural properties ===

*Shrine grove of Ōmiwa Shrine<ref>{{Cite web|和書|date= |url=http://www.pref.gifu.lg.jp/kyoiku-bunka-sports/bunka-geijutsu/bunkazai-zuroku/bunkazai-zuroku/tenki/oogakisi/oomiwa.html |title=Shrine grove of Ōmiwa Shrine |publisher=Gifu Prefecture |accessdate=2013-04-25}}</ref>

=== Access ===
*From {{ill|Sekigahara Station|Q872034|qid=Q872034}} on the {{ill|Tōkaidō Main Line|Q1190152|qid=Q1190152}}, take the {{ill|Meihan Kintetsu Bus|Q11415818|qid=Q11415818}} Sekigahara-Toki line and get off at “Miya.”

=== Nearby facilities ===
*{{ill|Nishitakagike Jin'ya|Q11630008|qid=Q11630008}}

=== Other ===
*Shrine tradition gives the founding year as Shuchō 6, but that year does not exist. Since Shuchō 1 is {{ill|686|Q30619|qid=Q30619}}, “Shuchō 6” is estimated around {{ill|691|Q23474|qid=Q23474}}, suggesting a late 7th-century foundation.
*The current site is in former Ishi District, Mino Province. It moved here in Eiwa 7; before that it is said to have been at a place called Uenoyama.
